title: Evolutionary Mahalanobis Distance-Based Oversampling for Multi-Class Imbalanced Data Classification
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: no (Tables 1 and 6, pp. 13 and 16: all classes kept; Pavg and MAUC averaged over all p classes, pp. 13-14)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): y (p. 12): case B seeds are only borderline class-j points (at least one of the m Mahalanobis neighbours from another class); case A has no seed, points are drawn inside the ellipsoid (p. 11)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 4, 11): per class N_max/IR - |S_j| (eq. 1), split over ellipsoids by weight beta = inverse density x class purity (eqs. 32-34)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 12-13): m = 5 nearest neighbours inside the same ellipsoid by Mahalanobis distance with the ellipsoid matrix M_n (eq. 41)
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 11-12): case A random coordinates along the ellipsoid eigen-axes, rescaled by kappa1 if outside (eqs. 37-40); case B x_k + kappa2 (x_k - x_l), kappa2 in [0,1] (eq. 42)
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): n (p. 12): no synthetic point is discarded; out-of-ellipsoid candidates are shrunk inside (eq. 40), which is part of placement
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n (pp. 7, 13): generated once, then C4.5; MOPSO and GKA fit the ellipsoids with geometric objectives (total size, coverage error; eqs. 17-19), no classifier in the loop
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: n (p. 11): other-class points inside an ellipsoid are called noise but are neither removed nor moved
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n (p. 13): five nearest neighbours fixed for case B; only the number of ellipsoids is chosen from the data (Sect. 4, p. 10)
notes: Multiclass handling: one ellipsoid model per minority class, fitted class j vs all other classes (F2, eq. 18, p. 7); each class oversampled to N_max/IR independently, no class order. FLAG: in 5 of 9 Table 1 sets only one class qualifies and is oversampled (Balance, Hayes-Roth, Breast-Tissue, UKM, Vertebral; p. 13). Partial because interpolation is only the fallback for ellipsoids with purity < 0.9: "Borderline SMOTE [30] is modified to generate synthetic samples in this case" (p. 12). FLAG: eq. 42 as printed points away from x_l although the text says "random interpolation" (p. 12). "The minority class with the minimum size was selected to validate the effectiveness" (p. 13) refers to the Pmin and AUCm metrics.

title: KNNOR: An oversampling technique for imbalanced datasets
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes (p. 11): KEEL sets built from multiclass UCI sources, smaller classes as minority and the remaining classes merged as majority (Sect. 4.1); CIFAR-10 airplane vs rest (p. 14)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): y (p. 4): only the top d% of minority points, ranked by distance to their k-th nearest minority neighbour, are seeds (Alg. 1); d is set from the knee of the smoothed distance curve (Alg. 1a, Sect. 3.1.1)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): n (p. 7): Alg. 2 loops over the kept seeds (densest first), one accepted point per seed per pass, until aug_num points are accepted
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 6-7): all k nearest minority neighbours of the origin are used in order of closeness, chained (eq. 5, Alg. 2), instead of one drawn at random
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 6-8): k chained steps, each from the previous synthetic point toward the next neighbour of the origin by a random fraction in [0, alpha]; alpha capped by the minimum minority-majority distance (eqs. 5-8, Alg. 2a)
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): y (p. 8): a candidate is kept only if all its k nearest neighbours are minority, otherwise discarded (Alg. 3, Sect. 3.3)
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n (p. 11): oversampling, then kNN/SVM/DT/MLP in repeated stratified 5-fold CV (Sect. 4.3)
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: n (pp. 4-6): points beyond the threshold are only left out of seeding; no original example is removed
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n (pp. 4, 11): k is a user input (Alg. 1), varied over random parameter combinations (Sect. 4.2); only d and alpha are set from the data
notes: C3 n: filtered points "will not be used in the consequent augmentation steps" (Fig. 7 caption, p. 6). FLAG: eqs. 1 and 6-8 print x + (x - x_near) alpha, pointing away from the neighbour, but Alg. 2 places the point "on a line joining source and n" (p. 7); read as interpolation, so the final point is a chained convex-type combination of the origin and its k neighbours. FLAG: text says "the points closest to their kth nearest neighbor get higher priority" (p. 6), but Alg. 2 gives each kept seed one point per pass, so allocation coded n. Future work only: "applying the algorithm on each of the minority datasets" (p. 16).

title: Noise-robust oversampling for imbalanced data classification
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes for the binary runs: D1-D10 are KEEL one-vs-rest or x-vs-y splits (Yeast-8 vs 2, Ecoli-5 vs 0-6-7, Page-blocks-4 vs 1-3, Yeast4, etc.; supp. p. 11); no for the 20 multiclass sets (all classes kept, Table 2, p. 7)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): n (supp. p. 6; p. 4): every minority sample is a seed (supp. Alg. 3 step 9); seeds are typed inland, borderline or trapped by CFSFDP clusters and local density (Sect. 3.2), and the type picks the generator
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): y (supp. p. 6): zeta(x_i) proportional to (1 - rho(x_i)) x theta x (|X_maj| - |X_min|) (supp. Alg. 3 steps 4-8); multiclass: theta x gap to the largest class (supp. p. 8)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): y (p. 5; supp. pp. 4, 6): inland seeds take a random partner from their whole CFSFDP cluster; borderline seeds a random one of their k6 nearest majority neighbours; HEEM distance for mixed data (eqs. 5-6)
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): y (p. 5; supp. pp. 3, 7): trapped seeds get points from adaptive embedding, gradient minimisation of association and diversity losses (eqs. 2-4, supp. Alg. 2); categorical values chosen under VDM constraints (supp. Alg. 4); inland and borderline use s = x_i + gamma (x_j - x_i), gamma range not stated
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 3, 6): after oversampling the binary version removes borderline and trapped majority samples (Alg. 1 steps 4-6); the multiclass version removes inland samples of the class-overlap set R, original or synthetic (Sect. 4.2.2; supp. Alg. 5, supp. p. 7)
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n (supp. p. 13): oversampling and cleaning run once on each training fold (2-fold CV x 5), then C5.0/MLP/KNN/NB (SVM for the binary runs, p. 10)
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: y (pp. 3, 6): removes majority borderline and trapped samples (binary) and inland samples of overlap regions (multiclass)
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n (supp. p. 15): k1-k6 are parameters searched over 1-10 (supp. Table 4); inland partners come from the whole cluster, not a kNN
notes: FLAG variants: binary noise-robust algorithm (Alg. 1) = B; multiclass and mixed-type NROMM (supp. Alg. 6) = M; paper as a whole = B+M. Section 3: "we first summarize our NROMM for binary and numerical imbalanced data classification" (p. 3). Multiclass handling: classes sorted by size; each class except the largest is oversampled one at a time against the original and synthetic samples of all larger classes (one-versus-ensemble), smaller classes set aside (Sect. 4.2.1, Fig. 4, p. 6); target theta x gap to the largest class (theta = 1 in supp. Table 3, supp. p. 13); overlap cleaning after all classes. FLAG Core vs Partial: "we employ the interpolation method to generate SI and SB" (p. 5), but trapped seeds use the non-interpolating embedding. Embedding also updates T and M internally, but only S_T is returned (supp. Alg. 2).

title: RSMOTE: A self-adaptive robust SMOTE for imbalanced problems with label noise
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes for the binary runs (not described): Table 2 sizes match one-class-vs-rest splits of multiclass UCI sets (iris 100/50, wine 107/71, vehicle 647/199, segment 1980/330; p. 409); no for the 8 multiclass sets (all classes kept, p. 416)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 402-403): minority points whose k nearest neighbours are all majority are treated as noise and get no synthetic points (Step 1; Alg. 1 lines 3-12)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 402-403): total N split over the safe and borderline clusters by cluster size, then per seed by w_i = (k - m)/(k + 1), normalised (Step 3; Alg. 1 lines 16-21)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): y (p. 402): new samples are generated "within each cluster", so partners come from the seed's own safe or borderline cluster (Step 3); scope of nnarray not stated (flag)
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): n (p. 402): SMOTE's Populate, random point on the segment
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n (pp. 408-409, 415): oversample the 75% training split once, then AdaBoost/LR/DT/KNN/GBDT (DOVO for multiclass)
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: n (p. 416): noisy minority points are only skipped as seeds; nothing is removed from the original data
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n (p. 409): knn enumerated in {3, 5, 20} to find the best result; "self-adaptive" refers to the 2-means split of relative density (pp. 401-402), not to k
notes: Multiclass handling: classes sorted by size; each class smaller than the largest class Y_s is balanced to n_s, "call RSMOTE to balance the class Y_t with respect to class Y_s" (p. 414); relative density computed per class; classifier is DOVO, one-against-one with a per-pair learner (p. 415). FLAG: not stated whether heterogeneous neighbours come from Y_s only or from all other classes. FLAG neighbour choice: p. 404 says the kNN used for relative density "are the same as the k-nearest neighbors used in the interpolating procedure". C3 evidence: "none of the oversampling methods filter any noisy samples from the original data" (p. 416), although p. 402 says it keeps minority samples "except for the noisy ones".

title: Safe-Level-SMOTE: Safe-Level-Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling TEchnique for Handling the Class Imbalanced Problem
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes (p. 480): Satimage class 4 taken as minority and the remaining classes merged as majority
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 478-479): no synthetic point when seed p and its drawn neighbour n both have safe level 0 (case 1, Fig. 1 lines 12-14); otherwise every positive is a seed
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): n (p. 479): one synthetic point per positive instance per pass, |D| - t in total (Fig. 1 line 2)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): n (pp. 479-480): one of the k = 5 nearest positive neighbours drawn at random (Fig. 1 line 3)
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): y (pp. 478-479): gap range set by the safe-level ratio: [0,1] if equal, [0, 1/ratio] if ratio > 1, [1 - ratio, 1] if ratio < 1, gap = 0 (copy of p) when n has safe level 0 (Fig. 1 lines 16-30)
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n (p. 480): oversampled data given to C4.5, Naive Bayes and SVM under 10-fold CV
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: n (p. 479): returns only the synthetic set D'; original instances untouched
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n (p. 480): k = 5 in all over-sampling techniques
notes: FLAG seed selection y is a judgement call: in case 1 the "synthetic instance will not be generated because the algorithm does not want to emphasize" noise (p. 478); a seed with safe level 0 and a safer partner gets ratio 0, so gap = 1 and s copies n (p. 479). Safe level = positives among the k nearest neighbours in the whole data (formula 7, p. 478). Gap is drawn per attribute inside the loop (Fig. 1, p. 479), as in SMOTE's own pseudocode.
